course.title: When does late notice cost a party its claim?
course.scope: One classroom comparison of the two notice clauses and the decision on River.
course.jurisdiction: unknown; fictional exercise, no background law assumed
course.audience: students who missed the contracts seminar

inputs.kind: transcript and handout in one packet

content_units.proposition: All parties and materials are fictional. No background law applies in the exercise.

locations.excerpt: Synthetic contracts seminar. All parties, documents, rules and decisions are invented for the exercise.

Teacher: In our first contract North promises to notify East promptly of a defect. The clause you have is the whole agreement about notice. It promises notice. Is a late claim automatically lost? That is a different question. We are not assuming any background law for today's exercise.

content_units.proposition: Friday 16:50 dispatch preceded the cutoff; Monday 09:00 delivery failed timely receipt.

locations.excerpt: Teacher: River's courier left on Friday at 16:50. Delivery was Monday at 09:00. The panel decided one ground. You don't have to guess what it would have done on the signature.
“A claim lapses unless signed notice reaches the buyer by Friday at 17:00.”

chapters.learning_object: Distinguish failure to give prompt notice from a stated condition for retaining a claim.
relations: Compare promised performance with the consequence the clause specifies.
Connect the verb reaches with receipt and compare its actual time to the cutoff.
Separate the panel’s sole ground from a possible ground it reserved.
prerequisites: Locate the parties, relevant action and exact wording in each clause.
chapters.approach: Start with the student's analogy and resolve it with a close reading of the two clauses and the decision.
chapters.role: Standalone seminar for the two examples.

terms.decision: Use for the claim consequence expressed in River’s clause.
Treat as receipt by the buyer, identified separately from courier departure.
